data.topic: Fix memory/correction pipeline bugs from AUDIT.md: BUG-5 (non-atomic budget enforcement in om_write.py), BUG-6 (decision shadows set feedback_score=0 causing immediate pruning), BUG-10 (wrong dirname count in signal_processor.py/stop_processor.py), BUG-11 (prune_expired kills score=0 entries immediately), R-7 (double correction detection in stop_processor), CQ-6 (duplicated signal processing logic), CQ-10 (misnamed simhash function)
data.what: Fix 7 bugs and code quality issues in the memory/correction pipeline identified by the code audit
in_scope: BUG-5: Make budget enforcement atomic with insert in om_write.py
BUG-6: Fix decision shadow feedback_score=0 in tools_knowledge.py — use om_write() or set non-zero score
BUG-10: Fix dirname count in signal_processor.py and stop_processor.py (2 not 3)
BUG-11: Skip pruning for feedback_score=0 entries in om_write.py
R-7: Remove duplicate process_session_corrections call from stage_signal_processing in stop_processor.py
CQ-6: Extract shared logic from stop_processor/signal_processor into signal_processor.main_logic()
out_of_scope: Hook shell injection fixes (BUG-1, BUG-2) — separate presearch
SQLite concurrency fixes (BUG-3, BUG-4) — separate presearch
PM tool bugs (BUG-7, BUG-8, BUG-9) — separate presearch
data.problem: Memory pipeline has multiple correctness bugs: decision shadows are immediately pruned (feedback_score=0), budget enforcement is non-atomic (data loss on crash), correction counts are doubled per session, project root is computed wrong (breaks auto-distillation), and simhash function is misnamed
data.why: The semantic memory persistence guarantee is hollow — pm_add_decision writes entries that get pruned within 24 hours. Correction counts are inflated, causing premature preference promotion. Auto-distillation looks in the wrong directory.
data.end_goal: All 7 issues fixed, memory pipeline correctly persists decisions, counts corrections once, and computes correct paths
data.complexity_reasoning: All bugs have exact file/line locations in code we own — pure internal fixes requiring no external research
